records.gloss: For the director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.
pieces: For the music director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.

L.1: For the director: a maskil of the sons of Korah.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of the family of Korah, to teach and give insight.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: maskil: a song of insight, or a skillful song
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to have insight, act wisely" (41:2). As a heading for thirteen psalms it may mark a song that teaches, or one composed with skill; its exact sense is no longer known.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a guild of temple singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as singers in the temple (2 Chronicles 20:19). Psalms 42-49 and 84-88 bear their name.

decisions.choice: Psalms 42 and 43 are one poem
decisions.reason: The two psalms share a refrain (42:6, 42:12, 43:5) and the line "Why do I go about mourning ..." (42:10; 43:2), and Psalm 43 has no title, so they were first one song. Psalm 42 also opens Book Two of the Psalms (Psalms 42-72).

decisions.choice: a song of the family of Korah, to teach and give insight
alternatives: a maskil of the sons of Korah
decisions.reason: Readable gives the likely sense of maskil (m2) and says what "sons" means here.

records.heading: Thirsty for the living God

records.source: כְּאַיָּ֗ל תַּעֲרֹ֥ג עַל־אֲפִֽיקֵי־מָ֑יִם כֵּ֤ן נַפְשִׁ֨י תַעֲרֹ֖ג אֵלֶ֣יךָ אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: As a deer longs for channels of water, so my soul longs for you, God.
pieces: Like a doe that longs for running streams, I long for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God, with all my being.

L.2: As a deer longs for channels of water, so my soul longs for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God.

R.2: A deer is thirsty and looks for a stream of water. In the same way, God, I am longing for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: longs: cries out with thirst
decisions.reason: The verb ('arag) is found only here and in Joel 1:20, where animals cry out to God for water in a drought. It is longing that can be heard.

decisions.choice: a deer: perhaps a doe
decisions.reason: The noun is masculine but the verb is feminine, so the animal may be a doe.

decisions.choice: my soul: my whole self, thirsting
decisions.reason: Nefesh can also mean the throat; the picture of thirst is felt in the whole person.

decisions.choice: God: the name used in Book Two
decisions.reason: In Psalms 42-83 the general word for God ('elohim) is used far more often than the divine name. Psalm 42 uses the name only once (verse 9).

decisions.choice: I (with all my being)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "I" for nefesh here, as the convention allows.

records.source: צָמְאָ֬ה נַפְשִׁ֨י׀לֵאלֹהִים֮ לְאֵ֪ל חָ֥י מָתַ֥י אָב֑וֹא וְ֝אֵרָאֶ֗ה פְּנֵ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: My soul thirsts for God, for [the] God living; when will I come and appear [before] the face of God?
pieces: I am thirsty for God, the living God. When may I come and stand before God's face?

L.3: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God; when will I come and appear before the face of God?

R.3: I am thirsty for God, the God who is alive. When can I go to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house and be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again?

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: God ('el) who is alive and acts, unlike idols (84:3; Joshua 3:10). The thirst is for God himself, as living water (Jeremiah 2:13).

decisions.choice: appear before the face of God
decisions.reason: The vowels of the Hebrew text read "appear before", the phrase used for coming to the sanctuary at the festivals (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The same letters could be read "see the face of God", and some ancient translations do so. The meaning is close: to come into God's presence in his house.

decisions.choice: to his house
decisions.reason: Readable says where one appears before God's face (m2).

records.source: הָֽיְתָה־לִּ֬י דִמְעָתִ֣י לֶ֭חֶם יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה בֶּאֱמֹ֥ר אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: My tears have been to me [my] bread by day and night, while [they] say to me all the day, Where [is] your God?
pieces: Day and night I have fed on my tears, while all day long people ask me, "Where is your God?"

L.4: My tears have been my bread by day and night, while [they] say to me all the day, "Where [is] your God?"

R.4: I cry all day and all night; tears are all I have to eat. All day long people ask me, "Where is your God?"

decisions.choice: my tears have been my bread: I have wept instead of eating
decisions.reason: His grief is so great that tears are his only food (80:6; 102:10).

decisions.choice: Where is your God?: a mocking question
decisions.reason: People ask it to mock, as if his God had left him or did not exist (79:10; 115:2).

records.source: אֵ֤לֶּה אֶזְכְּרָ֨ה׀וְאֶשְׁפְּכָ֬ה עָלַ֨י׀נַפְשִׁ֗י כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר׀בַּסָּךְ֮ אֶדַּדֵּ֗ם עַד־בֵּ֥ית אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים בְּקוֹל־רִנָּ֥ה וְתוֹדָ֗ה הָמ֥וֹן חוֹגֵֽג׃
records.gloss: These I remember, and I pour out on me my soul: that I used to pass along with the throng; I led them in procession to [the] house of God, with [the] sound of a joyful shout and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.
pieces: I pour out my heart as I call these things to mind: how I walked with the crowd and led them up to God's house, among shouts of joy and songs of thanks, a great crowd celebrating the feast.

L.5: These [things] I remember, and I pour out my soul within me: how I used to go along with the throng, leading them in procession to the house of God, with the sound of a joyful shout and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.

R.5: My heart breaks when I remember how things used to be. I used to walk with the crowds to God's house. I led them as they went. We shouted for joy and sang songs of thanks. A huge crowd was celebrating the festival.

decisions.choice: I pour out my soul: I let all my grief out
decisions.reason: To pour out the soul or the heart is to spill out one's grief before God (62:9; 1 Samuel 1:15).

decisions.choice: the throng; I led them in procession
alternatives: in the shelter (of the Mighty One)
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. The first (sakh) seems to mean a crowd; the second (eddaddem) seems to mean leading or walking with them at a festival pace. The ancient Greek translation read the line quite differently.

decisions.choice: a multitude keeping festival: the pilgrim feasts
decisions.reason: Three times a year Israel went up to the sanctuary for the feasts (Deuteronomy 16:16). The verb (chagag) is to keep such a festival with joy.

decisions.choice: My heart breaks
decisions.reason: Readable gives the feeling behind the picture (m1).

records.source: מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀נַפְשִׁי֮ וַתֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֥וֹד אוֹדֶ֗נּוּ יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and you are in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to him [for the] salvation of his face.
pieces: Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} thanks again, for the rescue that comes from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence.

L.6: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and [why] are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, [for] the salvation of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face.

R.6: I tell myself: Why are you so sad? Why are you so upset? Keep hoping in God! I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is with me, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saves me.

decisions.choice: my soul: the psalmist speaks to himself
decisions.reason: The refrain is a conversation inside the psalmist: one part of him asks why his soul is so low and urges it to hope. Soul (nefesh) is the whole self, here his own heart.

decisions.choice: bowed down, in turmoil: crushed and restless
decisions.reason: The first verb (shachach) is to be bent low, sunk down; the second (hamah) is the roaring or restlessness of the sea, which the poem pictures in 42:8.

decisions.choice: the salvation of his face
alternatives: the salvation of my face, and my God (as in 42:12 and 43:5)
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text has "the salvation of his face", that is, the help that comes from God's presence. In the other two refrains it reads "the salvation of my face, and my God". Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations read the refrain here as there, joining "my God" from the start of verse 7. The Hebrew text as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: why
decisions.reason: The second "why" of the other refrains is not repeated here; it is understood (bracketed at Literal).

decisions.choice: I tell myself: Why are you ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he is speaking to himself (m1).

records.source: אֱֽלֹהַ֗י עָלַי֮ נַפְשִׁ֪י תִשְׁתּ֫וֹחָ֥ח עַל־כֵּ֗ן אֶ֭זְכָּרְךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ יַרְדֵּ֑ן וְ֝חֶרְמוֹנִ֗ים מֵהַ֥ר מִצְעָֽר׃
records.gloss: My God, within me my soul is bowed down; therefore I remember you from [the] land of Jordan and Hermons, from Mount Mizar.
pieces: My God, I am bent low inside; so I will remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here in the Jordan country and on the peaks of Hermon, on Mount Mizar.

L.7: My God, my soul is bowed down within me; therefore I remember {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} from the land of [the] Jordan and [the] Hermons, from Mount Mizar.

R.7: My God, I feel so sad. So I think about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here, far away in the north, where the Jordan River begins, near Mount Hermon and Mount Mizar.

decisions.choice: the Jordan and the Hermons: far from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Jordan rises at the foot of Mount Hermon, in the far north of the land. The Hermons are its peaks. The poet is far from the temple, among the mountains and rushing water of the next verse.

decisions.choice: Mizar: a hill whose place is unknown
decisions.reason: The name means "little" and is otherwise unknown; it may be a small peak near Hermon, set against the great mountain.

decisions.choice: therefore I remember you: memory against despair
decisions.reason: Because he is low, he turns his mind to God, answering the refrain's question. "My God" at the start may belong to the end of verse 6 (see the note there).

decisions.choice: far away in the north
decisions.reason: Readable says where these places are (m1).

records.source: תְּהֽוֹם־אֶל־תְּה֣וֹם ק֭וֹרֵא לְק֣וֹל צִנּוֹרֶ֑יךָ כָּֽל־מִשְׁבָּרֶ֥יךָ וְ֝גַלֶּ֗יךָ עָלַ֥י עָבָֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: Deep to deep is calling at [the] sound of your waterfalls; all your breakers and your waves over me have passed.
pieces: One deep calls out to another at the roar of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cascades; all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breaking waves and rollers have gone over my head.

L.8: Deep calls to deep at the sound of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waterfalls; all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} breakers and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waves have passed over me.

R.8: Your waterfalls roar, and the deep waters call to each other. It is as if {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} waves are crashing over me, and I am drowning.

decisions.choice: deep to deep: the great waters
decisions.reason: The deep (tehom) is the mass of water of Genesis 1:2. In the north the poet hears torrents roaring, and they become a picture of the troubles that overwhelm him.

decisions.choice: your waterfalls
decisions.reason: The word (tsinnor) is rare and may mean a channel or rush of water.

decisions.choice: your breakers, your waves: trouble that God allows
decisions.reason: He calls the waves God's: even his distress is under God's hand (88:8). The words are echoed in Jonah's prayer from the sea (Jonah 2).

decisions.choice: It is as if ... I am drowning
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison and says what it means.

records.source: יוֹמָ֤ם׀יְצַוֶּ֬ה יְהוָ֨ה׀חַסְדּ֗וֹ וּ֭בַלַּיְלָה שִׁיר֣וֹ עִמִּ֑י תְּ֝פִלָּ֗ה לְאֵ֣ל חַיָּֽי׃
records.gloss: By day YHWH commands his loyal love, and in the night his song [is] with me, a prayer to [the] God of my life.
pieces: By day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and at night {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} song stays with me, a prayer to the God who gives me life.

L.9: By day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commands {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love, and in the night {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} song [is] with me, a prayer to the God of my life.

R.9: During the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows me {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love. At night I sing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and pray to God, who keeps me alive.

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: As in 40:11 (chesed).

decisions.choice: commands: sends out, or may he send out
alternatives: May the LORD command his loyal love
decisions.reason: The LORD gives an order and his loyal love goes out like a messenger (compare 43:3). The verb can also be a wish.

decisions.choice: his song: a song about him, sung at night
decisions.reason: "His song" is the song he gives or the song in his praise. Day and night together mean all the time.

decisions.choice: the LORD: the divine name, once in the poem
decisions.reason: The divine name appears only here in Psalms 42-43.

records.source: אוֹמְרָ֤ה׀לְאֵ֥ל סַלְעִי֮ לָמָ֪ה שְׁכַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה־קֹדֵ֥ר אֵלֵ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב׃
records.gloss: I will say to God my rock, Why have you forgotten me? Why mourning do I walk about in [the] oppression of an enemy?
pieces: I cry out to God, my rock: "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put me out of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mind? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?"

L.10: I will say to God my rock, "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgotten me? Why do I walk about mourning under the oppression of an enemy?"

R.10: God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are my rock. So I ask {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, "Why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forgotten me? Why am I so sad? Why do my enemies treat me so badly?"

decisions.choice: my rock: my safe place
decisions.reason: A high rock is a place of safety from enemies (18:3; 31:4).

decisions.choice: mourning: dressed in dark clothes of grief
decisions.reason: The word (qoder) is to be dark or dirty, as mourners were, in sackcloth and ashes (35:14; 38:7).

decisions.choice: the same question in 43:2
decisions.reason: The second question is repeated almost word for word in 43:2, one of the signs that the two psalms are one poem.

records.source: בְּרֶ֤צַח׀בְּֽעַצְמוֹתַ֗י חֵרְפ֥וּנִי צוֹרְרָ֑י בְּאָמְרָ֥ם אֵלַ֥י כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם אַיֵּ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: With a shattering in my bones my foes have taunted me, when they say to me all the day, Where [is] your God?
pieces: My foes mock me with a taunt that crushes my bones, while all day long they ask me, "Where is your God?"

L.11: With a crushing in my bones my foes taunt me, while they say to me all the day, "Where [is] your God?"

R.11: My enemies make fun of me, and it hurts me deep inside, as if my bones were broken. All day long they ask me, "Where is your God?"

decisions.choice: a shattering in my bones: pain that goes to the bone
alternatives: as with a sword in my bones
decisions.reason: The word (retsach) is used elsewhere of murder; here it is a deadly blow felt in the bones, the frame of the whole person (6:3).

decisions.choice: Where is your God?
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: מַה־תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י׀נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה־תֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי־ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי׃
records.gloss: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to him, [the] salvation of my face and my God.
pieces: Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.

L.12: Why are you bowed down, my soul, and why are you in turmoil within me? Wait for God, for I will yet give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the salvation of my face and my God.

R.12: I tell myself: Why are you so sad? Why are you so upset? Keep hoping in God! I will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again. He saves me. He is my God.

decisions.choice: my soul: the psalmist speaks to himself
decisions.reason: The refrain is a conversation inside the psalmist: one part of him asks why his soul is so low and urges it to hope. Soul (nefesh) is the whole self, here his own heart.

decisions.choice: bowed down, in turmoil: crushed and restless
decisions.reason: The first verb (shachach) is to be bent low, sunk down; the second (hamah) is the roaring or restlessness of the sea, which the poem pictures in 42:8.

decisions.choice: the salvation of my face: the one who saves me in person
decisions.reason: The plural "salvations" (yeshu'ot) means full rescue. "My face" stands for the person: God is the one who saves him and lifts his face again.

decisions.choice: I tell myself: Why are you ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he is speaking to himself (m1).

decisions.choice: the refrain again
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, but the Hebrew here ends "the salvation of my face and my God"; 43:5 repeats these words exactly.
